easy.explanation: The verse says, “Then came David to Nob.”
David came to Ahimelech the priest.
The verse says that Ahimelech “was afraid at the meeting of David.”
easy.q: How did Ahimelech feel when he met David?

medium.explanation: Ahimelech asked David why he was alone and had no man with him.
medium.q: Why was Ahimelech surprised by David’s arrival?

medium.explanation: Ahimelech noticed that David had no men with him.
medium.q: What does the word “alone” mean in this verse?

medium.explanation: Ahimelech asked, “Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?”
medium.q: Which question did Ahimelech ask David?

answers: David arrives, but he has no companions
David arrives with an army, but has no food
challenge.explanation: David comes to Nob alone, which causes Ahimelech to be afraid.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in the verse?

answers: It was an ordinary priestly duty
challenge.explanation: Ahimelech’s fear and question show that David’s solitary arrival seemed unusual.
challenge.q: What does Ahimelech’s reaction suggest about David’s visit?

answers: He came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest
He came to Gath to Achish
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies both the place, Nob, and the person, Ahimelech the priest.
challenge.q: Which detail is specifically stated about David’s arrival?

easy.explanation: David said, “The king hath commanded me a business.”
easy.q: What did David say the king had commanded him?

easy.explanation: David asked for five loaves of bread or whatever was available.
easy.q: What did David ask Ahimelech to give him?

easy.explanation: Ahimelech said there was no common bread, but there was hallowed bread.
easy.q: What kind of bread was available?

answers: The king had commanded that no one know about it
He wanted to hide the bread
medium.explanation: David said the king had told him to let no man know anything about the business.
medium.q: Why did David describe his mission as secret?

answers: The young men had kept themselves from women
medium.explanation: The priest asked whether the young men had kept themselves from women.
medium.q: What condition did Ahimelech mention before giving the hallowed bread?

medium.explanation: David said, “the vessels of the young men are holy.”
medium.q: What did David say about the young men’s vessels?

answers: David asks for bread, Ahimelech explains the supply, and David answers about purity
Ahimelech offers a sword, and David asks for bread
David takes common bread and later requests hallowed bread
challenge.explanation: This is the order of the conversation in the passage.
challenge.q: What sequence best describes the discussion about the bread?

answers: It was the shewbread taken from before the Lord
It had been brought from Gath
It belonged to the young men
challenge.explanation: The passage says there was no bread except the shewbread taken from before the Lord.
challenge.q: Why was the bread not ordinary bread?

answers: The men had been kept from women and the mission was urgent
The men were hungry after a feast
The men had taken the bread before
challenge.explanation: David declares the men’s purity and explains the urgency of the situation.
challenge.q: What does David emphasize in his reply to Ahimelech?

easy.explanation: The verse says that a certain man named Doeg was there.
Doeg is identified as an Edomite.
The verse calls him a servant of Saul.

answers: He was chiefest of the herdmen
He was a soldier at the gate
medium.explanation: The verse calls him “the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.”
medium.q: What was Doeg’s position among Saul’s servants?

medium.explanation: Herdmen were those responsible for tending animals.
medium.q: What does “herdmen” refer to in this context?

answers: He was Saul’s servant and witnessed what happened
challenge.explanation: His position and presence gave him knowledge of the meeting.
challenge.q: Why might Doeg’s presence be important to the later story?

answers: He belonged to Saul and was chiefest among the herdmen
He was a priest and carried the shewbread
He was a Philistine king and a soldier
challenge.explanation: Both details are stated in the verse.
challenge.q: Which two facts identify Doeg’s importance?

challenge.explanation: The verse identifies Doeg and his position but does not say that he spoke with David.
challenge.q: What is not stated about Doeg in this verse?

easy.explanation: David asked whether there was a spear or sword under Ahimelech’s hand.
easy.q: What weapon did David ask about?

easy.explanation: The priest had the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
David said, “There is none like that; give it me.”
easy.q: What did David say about the sword?

answers: He had given them to Ahimelech
medium.explanation: David said he had brought neither sword nor weapons because the king’s business required haste.
medium.q: Why did David say he had no sword or weapons?

answers: Wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod
At the gate of the city
medium.explanation: Ahimelech said it was wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod.
The sword is identified as Goliath’s, whom David slew in the valley of Elah.

answers: He takes the weapon of an enemy he once defeated
challenge.explanation: The sword belonged to Goliath, whom David had slain.
challenge.q: What symbolic meaning may David’s taking of the sword suggest?

answers: The sword was the only available weapon of its kind there
The priest owned many identical swords
challenge.explanation: Ahimelech explains that there was no other sword available at that place.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “there is no other save that here” emphasize?

answers: David urgently requests a weapon and receives Goliath’s sword
David returns Goliath’s sword to the Philistines
David refuses to carry any weapon

paragraphs.title: David Comes to Gath and Escapes by Deception

easy.explanation: David fled for fear of Saul.
David went to Achish the king of Gath.
David feigned himself mad in their hands.
easy.q: What did David pretend to be?

answers: The servants recognized him as the one praised for killing Philistines
medium.explanation: Achish’s servants recalled the song praising David for killing many Philistines.
medium.q: Why did David become afraid of Achish?

medium.explanation: The passage says David “scrabbled on the doors of the gate.”
medium.q: What did David do on the doors of the gate?

medium.explanation: The verse says he let his spittle fall down upon his beard.
medium.q: What did David let fall upon his beard?

answers: He was recognized, became afraid, pretended to be mad, and was rejected by Achish
He received bread, returned to Nob, and was protected by Saul
He fought Achish, captured Gath, and returned to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The passage presents these events in that order.
challenge.q: What sequence led to David’s escape?

answers: It reminded them that David had slain many Philistines
It praised David as a peaceful priest
It identified David as one of Achish’s servants
challenge.explanation: The song said, “Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.”
challenge.q: How did the servants’ song increase David’s danger?

answers: He believed David was mad and did not want him in his house
He wanted David to become king
He feared David had no weapons
challenge.explanation: Achish said he had no need of mad men and asked why David had been brought to him.
